extracted.intended_audience: NASA staff preparing official correspondence, letters, and memos
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and formatting rules for drafting NASA official correspondence (letters, memos, envelopes, enclosures, concurrences, and related administrative texts), including plain-language guidance, grammar/usage rules, and exact layout/filing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use action verbs / avoid nominals
rubrics_metrics.description: Expressions with embedded verbs (nominals) are difficult to read and make sentences longer; use shorter, more direct action verbs instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DO NOT SAY / SAY examples: 'give consideration to' → 'consider'; 'is applicable to' → 'applies to'; 'make payment' → 'pay'; 'give recognition to' → 'recognize'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid weak general verbs; 'hit the verbs'
rubrics_metrics.description: Weak writing uses general verbs that require extra words; use strong verbs that can 'do things'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DO NOT SAY / SAY examples: 'make preparations for' → 'prepare for'; 'make use of' → 'use'; 'is indicative of' → 'shows'; 'undertake an analysis' → 'analyze'; 'as stated in' → 'states'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid '-ion of', '-ment of', and 'ize of' constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid verbose nominalizations formed with -ion, -ment, or 'ize of' which lengthen sentences and obscure action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use plain words; prefer simple language
rubrics_metrics.description: Government writing should be dignified but rely on plain language; avoid jargon and pretentious expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DO NOT SAY / SAY examples: 'construct, fabricate' → 'make'; 'initiate, commence' → 'begin'; 'terminate' → 'end'; 'utilize' → 'use'; 'substantial portion' → 'large part'; 'afforded an opportunity' → 'allow'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit needless words; avoid wordy expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use compound prepositions and other wordy expressions when one or two words convey the meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DO NOT SAY / SAY examples: 'because of the fact that' → 'since (because)'; 'call your attention to the fact that' → 'remind you'; 'for the period of' → 'for'; 'in many cases' → 'often'; 'the fact that he had not succeeded' → 'his failure'; 'the question as to whether' → 'whether'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid redundancies / word pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use word pairs if the words have the same effect or if one includes the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word pairs to avoid: any and all; authorize and direct; cease and desist; each and every; full and complete; order and direct; means and includes; necessary and desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concrete words when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract words can be vague; prefer simple, concrete words to reduce ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: If you mean 'vehicles' use 'automobiles'; 'firearms' → 'rifles'; 'aircraft' → 'helicopters' (use the concrete term appropriate to meaning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid words that antagonize
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose words that do not make the wrong impression or repel readers; prefer words that attract favorable reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USE words like 'achieve, benefit, guarantee, reasonable, reliable, service, useful, you, please' RATHER THAN 'allege, blame, waste, alibi, impossible, liable, oversight, unfortunate, wrong'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know and use correctly: must, shall, will, should, may, may not
rubrics_metrics.description: Different auxiliary verbs convey obligation, permission, or prediction and must be used correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: 'Shall' imposes obligation to act (also used legally); 'Will' predicts future action; 'Must' imposes obligation/necessity; 'Should' implies obligation or preference but not absolute necessity; 'May' indicates permission; 'May not' indicates prohibition. Guidelines: a) Use 'will' to predict future action. b) Use 'must' to indicate obligation to act (especially in everyday speech). c) Use 'must' or 'shall' in legal/regulatory documents to indicate obligation. d) Do not use 'will' to indicate obligation to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid split infinitives when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: The split infinitive offends many readers; avoid splitting 'to' and the verb where reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Be sure to reply promptly to the invitation.' preferred over 'Be sure to promptly reply to the invitation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid noun sandwiches / noun clusters
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative writing overuses noun clusters; divide them with prepositions to clarify intended meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DO NOT SAY: 'Underground mine workers safety protection procedures development.' SAY: 'Development of underground procedures for the protection of the safety of mine workers.' or 'Development of procedures for the protection of the safety of workers in underground mines.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use gender-specific terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid gender-specific job titles and phrasing; use gender-neutral alternatives throughout correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DO NOT SAY / SAY examples: 'crewman' → 'crewmember'; 'draftsman' → 'drafter'; 'enlisted men' → 'enlisted personnel'; 'fireman' → 'firefighter'; 'foreman' → 'supervisor'; 'manhours' → 'hours worked'; 'manpower' → 'personnel, workforce'. Also avoid gendered phrasing: 'The Administrator or his designee' → 'The Administrator or the Administrator's designee.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Know difference between 'which' and 'that'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'That' is defining (restrictive) and 'which' is nondefining; correct usage can change meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If only some rocket engines ignited, say 'The engines that ignited.' If all ignited, say 'The engines which ignited.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary or complicated references in the text
rubrics_metrics.description: Many letters need no references; when responding, subordinate the reference to the main point and keep it concise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Wordy: 'This is in reply to your conversation with Dr. Jones on August 1, 1999, wherein you requested a copy of the Program Operating Plan, a copy of which is enclosed.' Concise: 'Enclosed is the Program Operating Plan you requested from Dr. Jones on August 1, 1999.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Include in the text any reference cited in the reference line
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reference is listed in the reference line, it must also be included or cited in the body text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acronym usage: spell out on first use and don't overuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use acronyms more than necessary; spell out the term the first time followed by the acronym in parentheses; capitalize first letters of words that form the acronym.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Flight Readiness Review (FRR)'. See Appendix H for guidance on acronyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid acronyms used only infrequently
rubrics_metrics.description: If an acronym appears only twice or infrequently, spell out the term every time or avoid the acronym entirely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer/Internet word usage and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow The Gregg Reference Manual (1998) Appendix B for computer/Internet terminology and apply specific capitalization/hyphenation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules: a) 'Internet' and 'Net'—initial cap I and N even within a sentence. b) 'World Wide Web' or 'WWW' or 'Web'—initial cap W even within a sentence. c) 'Web site' and 'Web page'—two words, initial cap W. d) 'Home Page'—capitalize when referring to a specific home page/title. e) 'E-mail'—always hyphenated; initial cap 'E' only when heading or sentence initial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use all-capital letters in e-mail messages
rubrics_metrics.description: All-caps in e-mail implies shouting and should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard business letter: follow chapter figures and guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Before preparing letters, study the figures in Chapter 3; these guidelines comprise standard features for correct NASA letter formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator's correspondence special instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence for the Office of the Administrator has specific preparation and control instructions (see Appendix A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stationery for correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare correspondence on official NASA insignia 'meatball' letterhead; use plain bond for succeeding pages; Appendix A has additional stationery guidelines for Administrator offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type/font usage in correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer larger pica font over elite; use script or italic only for occasional emphasis; do not type entire letters in script/italic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Font size may be reduced to prevent a memo from continuing onto a second page (memo-specific exception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ink color
rubrics_metrics.description: Use black or blue-black ink to type, date, and sign correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins for letters and memos
rubrics_metrics.description: Set left margin two spaces to the right of the printed 'Reply to Attn of:' (approx. 1.2 or 1 1/8 inches); right and bottom margins approx. 1 inch; top margin at 1 inch on second and succeeding pages; do not justify the right margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: File copies: maintain official record copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Always prepare an official record copy (preferred official 'yellow' copy); if yellow not possible prepare white copy marked 'Official File' or 'Official Record Copy'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If concurrences required, use NASA Form 1267 (or 1267A) for the first page of the official file copy. Prepare only copies required by distribution practices of your office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to Attn of: include writer's code
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer's organizational/mail code or mail stop must appear on all outgoing correspondence on the 'Reply to Attn of:' line; type only the writer's code in letters or numerals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dating correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Date the letter after it is signed; stamping the date is preferred; if typed, ensure type style matches the letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement: stamp/type at right margin across from 'Reply to Attn of:' (e.g., August 20, 1998). Do not use military style (20 Aug 1998) or ordinal endings like 'th' or 'st' (e.g., Aug 20th).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inside address format
rubrics_metrics.description: Type inside address at left margin three typing returns below 'Reply to Attn of:'; include addressee's full name and title; do not abbreviate names or use nicknames; if gender unknown, address by first and last name in salutation; single-space address and arrange in block style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address elements: Line1 Name; Line2 Title (if applicable); Line3 Company/Federal Agency/Organization; Line4 Delivery/Street Address; Line5 City, State, ZIP. Examples for Non-NASA, NASA, International addressees are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address line length and runover rules
rubrics_metrics.description: No line of the address should be longer than 3 inches; when runover occurs indent second line two spaces from left margin; limit address to seven lines in correspondence and on envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 7 for envelope placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address salutations and forms of address
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Appendix E Forms of Addresses for proper salutations for domestic and international addresses; incoming documents often contain correct address format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salutation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalized business letters require a salutation; reference Figures 3-1 and 3-2 and Appendix E for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body of letter: spacing, paragraphing, and hyphenation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use single-spaced text with double spacing between paragraphs; type paragraphs in block form; number/letter subparagraphs as shown in figures; hyphenate sparingly to ensure uniform right margin; avoid hyphenating more than two consecutive lines and avoid hyphenating at end of first or last full line of a paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid widows and orphans
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not begin a paragraph near the end of a page unless there is room for at least two lines; do not continue a paragraph on the following page unless two lines can be carried over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Figure 3-3 for instructions on numbering pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succeeding page formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Type succeeding pages on plain bond paper; starting with second page, type page number five lines from top, approx. 1 inch from right edge; continue body two lines below page number; allow same margins as first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Figure 3-3 for numbering examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complimentary close wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Sincerely,' for all NASA correspondence. Use 'Respectfully,' when the letter is addressed to the President of the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature block format
rubrics_metrics.description: Type signature information at left margin five typing returns below complimentary close; type name, title, and office of signing official; do not use Mr./Mrs./Ms./Dr. in signature block; indent runover title lines two spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided for single and multi-line titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-signature block arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: When two people must sign, arrange signature blocks side by side or one beneath the other; if side by side begin first at left margin and second at center; complimentary close should begin at left margin; when NASA is originating Agency put NASA official signature block at left margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate side-by-side and one-under-another formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting official signature rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If known before typing that an acting official will sign, type 'Acting' before the title in the signature block; if the letter is prepared for one signer but another signs, the signer will write 'for' in front of the typed name; mark courtesy copies with actual signer's name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enclosure notation and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When an enclosure accompanies a letter, type 'Enclosure' flush with left margin 2 lines below signer's name or title. Identify enclosures in the text in as few words as possible or by title; if more than one enclosure indicate number (e.g., '3 Enclosures').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If enclosures not identified in text list each enclosure on separate lines. Mark the first page of each enclosure with 'Enclosure' (Enclosure1, Enclosure 2). Ensure enclosure counts in notation match actual items enclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postscripts discouraged but permitted with rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Postscripts are discouraged but may be added to avoid retyping; type 'P.S.:' at left margin two typing returns below signer's name or title and then sign or initial the postscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If signer handwrites a postscript, type it on all copies or photocopy the original for the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material sent under separate cover notation
rubrics_metrics.description: When material is sent under separate cover, type 'Separate Cover:' at left margin two typing returns below signer's title or 'Enclosure' notation and list the material; send a copy of the letter with the material mailed under separate cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format: 'Separate Cover: Form Letters Handbook-10 Copies' etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtesy copies (cc:) formatting and ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Type 'cc:' at left margin two returns below signature block/enclosure/separate cover; single-space list of recipients below; use office/org codes; use titles (Dr., Mr., Ms.) on correspondence outside NASA; dual-column 'cc:' permitted when list too long.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred order: 1) Originator's addressees first; 2) Headquarters addressees next; 3) Centers' codes next; 4) Federal agencies next; 5) Non-Federal organizations last. Indicate '(w/o encls.)' for recipients not sent enclosures. Lists must be in alphabetical and numerical order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official record copy preparation and bcc rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Official record copy must include drafting info; use 'bcc:' on the official file copy when recipient does not need to know who received copies or to document office of record; never type 'bcc:' on the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include official file copy with Agency filing scheme number from NPR 1441.1C. Indicate '(w/o encl.)' for recipients not receiving enclosures. Dual-column 'bcc:' lists follow same guidelines as 'cc:'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification line on file copies (office/writer/typist/phone info)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the bottom of file copies of the signature page, type the mail code of preparing office, the writer's first initial and surname, the typist's initials, the date of typing, and the writer's telephone extension in a compact identification line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'F/JSmith:abd:2/20/97:1234'. If rewritten or retyped add a second identification line directly below the first (e.g., 'Rewritten:F/EJones:olr:2/28/97:1222'). Type full seven-digit phone number if center has more than one prefix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use agency filing scheme number on official file copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Type the official file number on all file copies per NPR 1441.1C Records Retention Schedules (Agency filing scheme for indexing files).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining and documenting concurrences
rubrics_metrics.description: If concurrences are required, use NASA Form 1267 (or 1267A) for the first page of the official file copy; type the codes and names of concurring officials in the concurrence blocks; those officials sign and date in the space provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The signature page should reflect cc's, bcc's, official file, reading file, and identification line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative concurrences documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: As an alternative to NASA Forms 1267/1267A, type the mail codes and names of concurring officials on the bottom of the yellow official file copy (first page); concurring officials sign and date in the space provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping when letters are rewritten or retyped
rubrics_metrics.description: Each time a letter is rewritten or retyped, add an updated identification line to the official record copy; include name of rewriter or typist's initials; replace and destroy previous copies except official yellow and marked-up copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark through previous official copy with a diagonal red line and staple that marked-up copy to the rewritten one. If someone else retyped, include that person's initials in the identification line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrence/Approval signature block format for multi-signature cases
rubrics_metrics.description: When concurring or approving officials must sign on an original letter or report, use formatted 'Concurrence:' and 'Approval:' blocks with lines for Name, Title, and Date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show labeled lines for signature, printed name/title, and date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble letters for signature per chapter figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble letters in accordance with the illustrations (Figure 3-1) so the signer can quickly identify and review pertinent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Appendix A for Administrator's correspondence packaging and special assembly instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Envelopes and mailing: follow Chapter 7 and consult Mail Manager
rubrics_metrics.description: See Chapter 7 for specific preparation instructions for envelopes and mailing; consult Center Mail Manager for mailing services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not type instructions on the letter indicating special handling or mailing services (e.g., 'Special Delivery', 'Certified', 'Registered'); consult Mail Manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpersonalized business letter format
rubrics_metrics.description: Use nonpersonalized business letter format when addressee's name is unknown or letter is addressed to an organization (with attention to an individual); follow figures in the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key features: Attention line generally follows first line of address; there is no salutation; type 'Subject:' and follow one-line subject guidance; avoid separate reference line unless necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention line usage in nonpersonalized letters
rubrics_metrics.description: In the nonpersonalized business letter, an attention line generally follows the first line of the address at the left margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line rules for nonpersonalized letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Type 'Subject:' at left margin three typing returns below last line of the address. One-line subjects are preferred. Keep subject short and state the main topic concisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If responding to a letter with a 'Subject:' line, use the same subject. If acronyms used, spell out the term followed by acronym in parentheses; if abbreviation used frequently in the letter, establish it in the subject line. Capitalize first letter of key words and omit articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference line rules in business letters/memos
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid a separate reference line except when it contributes to understanding or when there are many references; if used, type 'Ref:' at left margin two returns below subject followed by itemized listing of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviate items (e.g., numeric dates). List references as (a), (b), (c) single-spaced in chronological order with most recent first. See figures for layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal letter format and caption
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal letter format is based on the standard business letter but used solely for legal correspondence (Office of General Counsel, Inspector General, Patent Counsel). The legal letter includes a caption beginning with 'Re:' indented five spaces from left margin, used to cite the specific case (protest, patent, license).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If caption more than one line, begin succeeding lines flush with first line. Indent entire caption five spaces from the right margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-addressee letters format and originals/copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use format for multiple-addressee letters when sending identical letters to more than one individual (outside NASA or personalized formats within NASA); prepare an original letter for each recipient and only one official file copy; document addressee list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recipients need to know who received identical letters, type 'Identical letter to:' two returns below signature block and list recipients. If documenting on file copy when recipients do not need to know, type the list on the official file copy. Exception: when list mostly within NASA but includes some outside individuals use multiple-addressee memo format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble multiple-addressee packages for signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange letters and accompanying documents so the signer can quickly review all pertinent documents; follow Appendix A for administrator package assembly when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condolence letter policy and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare condolence letters for Administrator's signature upon notification of an employee's death (and as appropriate for former employees or immediate family members); the letter should be completed and mailed within 3 business days after notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCIC should be advised upon notification. The office to which the employee was assigned prepares the letter to the next of kin and a letter to the employee for Administrator's signature upon death of an immediate family member. OCIC initiates when office is ambiguous and may request supporting documentation. Administrator-signed condolence does not preclude other condolences from colleagues.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASA memo policy: memos for internal use only
rubrics_metrics.description: NASA policy is to use memos for internal use only; letters are used for external and formal communications (e.g., congratulations, retirement, condolence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before preparing memos, study figures in Chapter 4. Guidelines apply across NASA Centers including Headquarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard memo stationery, type, and ink
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare memos on official NASA letterhead; use plain bond for succeeding pages. Prefer larger type over smaller; use script/italic only for emphasis; do not type entire memos in script/italic. Use black or blue-black ink to type, stamp, and sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Font size may be reduced to avoid a memo continuing to a second page (exception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Memo margins, file copies, and identification (memo-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set margins like letters (left margin 1.2 inches from 'Reply to Attn of:'); always prepare an official record copy (yellow preferred); if concurrences required use NASA Form 1267/1267A for first page of official file copy; other copies per office requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memo TO/THRU/FROM formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Always type 'TO:', 'THRU:', and 'FROM:' in all caps. 'TO:' at left margin three returns below 'Reply to Attn of:'; seven spaces after 'TO:' type mail code and title of addressee. 'THRU:' used when endorsement prior to receipt is required; 'FROM:' includes mail code and title of signer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use titles as preferred; if an individual does not use a title it's acceptable to have memo from title to name or name to name using full name formatting (e.g., B/John A. Smith). Single-space between each 'THRU:' line addressee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memo subject and reference rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Type 'SUBJECT:' at left margin two typing returns below last line of 'FROM:' followed by subject; subject should concisely state main topic. Avoid reference line unless it contributes; if used type 'REF:' two returns below subject and list references itemized and abbreviated as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If acronyms used in subject spell out then acronym in parentheses; capitalize first letter of key words and do not use articles (a, an, the) in subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memo body formatting and one-paragraph memo rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Use single-spaced text with double spacing between paragraphs; type paragraphs in block form; hyphenate sparingly; do not begin paragraph near end of page unless room for at least two lines. One-paragraph memos of 10 lines or less may use double spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number and letter subparagraphs as shown in figures (see Figure 4-2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Memo succeeding pages and page numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Type succeeding pages of a memo on plain bond paper; beginning with second page, type the page number five lines from top approx. 1 inch left of the right edge; continue the body two lines below page number; use same margins as first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Figure 4-3 for examples (referenced in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Memo signature block rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Type signature information at left margin five typing returns below last line of text; type the name of the signing official only; do not use Mr./Mrs./Ms./Dr. in signature block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If acting official known before typing, type 'Acting' before title in 'FROM:' line. If memo prepared for one signer but actually signed by another, that signer will write 'for' in front of the typed name; mark courtesy copies with actual signer's name to record who signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memo enclosures rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Enclosures included with a memo are handled like letter enclosures: type 'Enclosure' flush left two lines below signature block; identify enclosures in text or list them if not identified; indicate number if more than one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of numbered and unnumbered enclosures provided; mark first page of each enclosure and ensure counts match.
